text:
olivia: paging — seeing a sharp spike of 500s on /api/v1/users during canary for release/2026-03-15_1100, started ~5m ago. canary is 10% traffic.
incident-bot: Incident detected: endpoint /api/v1/users returning 5xx > 12% for 4 minutes. Notified on-call: olivia.
marc: on it. grabbing logs and DB metrics. quick question: did the canary include the schema migration?
olivia: yes, deploy includes migration job uid=mg-20260315-usr-schema, ran at 11:02 UTC in canary.
tara: I see the migration job is stuck on primary db: waiting on lock, PG pid 48231. it's trying to add column "profile_v2" WITHOUT DEFAULT and an exclusive lock is blocking.
marc: that aligns with the errors. app is getting DB errors: "column profile_v2 does not exist" on read paths and write paths failing with serialization errors.
kevin: product impact — signup/user updates might be erroring for some customers. any estimate on how many?
elaine: Support: ~6 customers reported errors in last 10min (dashboard ticket links: https://support.internal/t/8421).
marc: stack trace from app: 
```
PG::UndefinedColumn: ERROR: column "profile_v2" does not exist
  File \"/srv/service/app/models/user.rb\", line 214 in `update_profile'
```

tara: migration is ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN profile_v2 jsonb; then a backfill (UPDATE users SET profile_v2 = ...) — backfill is the part holding a long transaction and blocking selects on index build.
olivia: can we kill the migration? what's the risk?
tara: if we cancel the migration mid-backfill we might leave table partially updated. but current state is higher customer impact. recommendation: kill migration, rollback deploy to previous release which doesn't reference profile_v2. then rerun migration in a safer offline backfill mode.
marc: agree — code already assumes profile_v2 exists for new endpoints in canary; killing migration + rollback is safest. steps: 1) stop canary traffic, 2) kill migration job, 3) rollback canary release to previous image, 4) verify /api/v1/users healthy.
olivia: I'm taking on-call actions: switching canary routing to 0% and promoting old canary image for the 10% bucket. doing now. :mechanical_arm:
incident-bot: Routing change applied: canary traffic set to 0% at 11:07:42 UTC by olivia.
marc: application logs show new requests are being routed to stable image now. starting to see 5xx rate drop from 18% -> 9%
tara: killing the migration job on the primary now (pg_cancel_backend 48231), then will follow with pg_terminate_backend if it doesn't stop.
sre-runbook-bot: Reminder: when terminating long-running DDL, ensure you have a recent full backup and alert DB team. Next step: snapshot created automatically at 11:08:05 UTC.
tara: pg_cancel_backend returned false, issuing pg_terminate_backend 48231. terminated.
marc: connection errors in app dropped significantly. still seeing a few 5xx from lingering requests.
elaine: Support: telling affected customers we're rolling back deploy and investigating — working on a short status update.
kevin: big question: why did migration run during canary without a fallback plan? we need a postmortem and an immediate temp policy: never run blocking backfills in canary window.
olivia: agreed. for now incident severity = SEV2 (customer impact, partial outage). taking handoff to SRE for post-incident follow-up.
marc: rolling back canary image now (deploy rollback command):
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service users-api --to-image users-api:2026-03-08-stable --canary-percent 10
```

incident-bot: Deploy rollback initiated by marc at 11:12:01 UTC.
marc: rollback succeeded, canary bucket now on stable image. health checks passing. 5xx rate down to 1.2% in last 2m.
tara: verifying DB state: migration process terminated, no active long transactions. but table users has partial profile_v2 for ~2% of rows — backfill didn't finish.
marc: app logs no longer throwing UndefinedColumn. prelim check: no new errors in the last 5m.
elaine: support update posted: "We've rolled back a recent canary that triggered DB errors for a subset of users. We're restoring normal service and will follow up once we understand root cause." :white_check_mark:
kevin: flagging this for immediate postmortem — action items: migration gating policy, run backfills offline, add pre-deploy DB lock checks, update runbook.
olivia: handing off to marc and tara for RCA — I'll remain on incident channel for the next hour for follow-up.
marc: recording timeline and metrics, will open an incident ticket and assign owners.
tara: plan for next steps: create dedicated backfill job that writes to a shadow column with batched transactions, add migration lock timeout, and ensure migrations run out-of-band from canary window.
incident-bot: Incident resolved? set to "monitoring" at 11:22:56 UTC by marc.
olivia: thanks everyone. will schedule a quick post-incident sync 30m from now. :coffee:
marc: adding runbook updates now and will link PR in incident ticket.
elaine: closing loop with support and CS. customer-facing post will go out after RCA drafts are ready.
